source.title: Stable initialization without the CLT
source.authors: Simon Kuang; Kyle R. Chickering; Xin-Fan Lin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The paper is a preprint.
record.tranche_reason: It compares initialization schemes and reports training loss for neural representation tasks, bearing on the initialization part of V4. It does not test the classification-error claims on CIFAR or the stated depth and learning-rate mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training MSE for image fitting under several initializations. Its audio and image evaluation metrics, width-scaling trends, and Jacobian spectra do not measure the training classification error or the specific mechanisms in V1–V6, so they are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares initialization recipes on coordinate regression, but does not establish faster learning or greater trainable depth as V4 specifies. Final fitting errors and initialization-time Jacobian moments measure related outcomes. The learning-rate sweep addresses width-dependent hyperparameter transfer without measuring V5's stability threshold or recovery trajectory.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors claim exact initialization-ensemble hidden-Jacobian second-moment guarantees at any width and depth, and competitive zero-shot input/output calibration. These guarantees do not establish stable individual Jacobian spectra or exact loss-gradient guarantees; Appendix A.3 requires an additional independence heuristic for loss gradients. Empirical superiority is conditional: SM20 fits the audio best and has lower wide-network image training MSE.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes uniform-phase sine initialization and moment-matched input/output layers, then compares it with prior sine initializations. Its experiments use coordinate-based regression and MSE, not classification training error.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization choice and width change the reported training MSE in the Cameraman image-fitting tables. Width-sweep loss curves are discussed, but the plotted time-averaged training MSE is not extracted as a claim-version row.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization rankings depend on width: SM20 has the lowest reported final training MSE at width 256, whereas uniform-phase MM has the lowest at width 16.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization choice affects fixed-budget coordinate-regression fitting error, with rankings that depend on width.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 1 preserves expected hidden-layer Jacobian Gramians at every width and depth; Appendix A.4 nevertheless reports spectral broadening with depth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Preserving ensemble-average squared Jacobian amplification does not ensure preservation of individual singular values.

fits_no_version.finding: The width/learning-rate sweep reports time-averaged training MSE. Under both tested µP scalings, optimal learning rates still shift with width, and last-layer rescaling makes little difference.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested µP prescriptions do not achieve optimal-learning-rate transfer across widths in these sinusoidal image-fitting networks.

record.problems: The reported training measures are MSE on image fitting rather than classification error. The initialization comparisons report no uncertainty estimates. The audio fitting uses the full signal for both optimization and evaluation, with no held-out split.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows were omitted. Evaluation MSE/SNR, audio fitting, width/learning-rate sweep curves, and Jacobian-spectrum diagnostics do not measure the training classification-error outcome or a mechanism named by a tested version.

untested.parts: Convolutional-network training classification error on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe conditions.
Spurious-local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and its reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation and its prevention by identity shortcuts or the specified initialization recipes.
Learning-speed and trainable-depth comparisons attributable to signal/gradient-preserving initialization; orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh networks and very deep convolutional training.
Initial stability thresholds, loss recovery above them, curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the initial threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on learning speed and tolerated learning rates, and Fixup residual-network comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: V4 does not require classification error, so MSE alone is not grounds for exclusion. The issue is the absence of a direct result on its specified speed or trainable-depth effect. Table 2's text extraction interleaves columns; R4 and R6 use evaluation values as training values.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, model size, and regularization/early stopping.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks, depth effects on training classification error, batch normalization, and the cited special initialization approaches.

Training speed and maximum trainable depth are not measured; the empirical comparisons use sine MLPs on image fitting at fixed depth, plus other activation baselines, rather than testing all initialization claims listed.
No stability limit or sharpness/curvature trajectory is measured, and the loss-sweep results do not test the stated above-stability recovery mechanism.
No batch-normalization comparison or normalization-free residual-network test.
